dimensions.assessment: Affects applicable tax-exempt charitable organizations engaging in fiscal sponsorship arrangements, organization managers, and contributors.
dimensions.evidence: applies to an organization to which subsection (b) applies, other than-- (A) a private foundation... or (B) a donor advised fund

dimensions.assessment: Imposes new IRS reporting obligations, significant excise taxes for improper conduit arrangements, and strips tax deductions for non-compliant contributions.
dimensions.evidence: there is hereby imposed on any amount transferred pursuant to an improper conduit arrangement a tax equal to 20 percent of the amount thereof.

dimensions.assessment: Creates potential excise tax revenues and affects federal tax deductions for contributions under improper conduit arrangements, though exact fiscal totals are unstated.
dimensions.evidence: disallows a federal tax deduction for contributions under such arrangements.

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 by adding new annual reporting items, definitions for fiscal sponsorships, excise tax structures, and rules for deduction disallowances.
dimensions.evidence: Section 6033(b) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking and at the end... and by inserting after paragraph (15) the following new paragraph

dimensions.assessment: Applies permanently to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this subsection shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027.

missing_information: Projected federal revenue changes or the exact volume of affected fiscal sponsorship arrangements are not specified.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires certain charitable organizations to report fiscal sponsorship arrangement details to the IRS, imposes excise taxes of 20% on organizations and 5% on managers for improper conduit arrangements, and disallows tax deductions for contributions made under such improper arrangements.
